chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever commits an injustice, he will be seized by it regarding his self, or his wealth, or his children.

key_terms.أُخِذَ بِهَا: seized by it / punished for it

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who commits injustice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the comprehensive scope of divine justice (adl), emphasizing that retribution for oppression may manifest in the self, wealth, or progeny. It reflects the Shia theological understanding that God’s justice is not limited to the afterlife but often manifests in this world through tangible consequences, serving as both a warning to the oppressor and a comfort to the oppressed.
